subject: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up
messages:
From: Alice Singh <alice.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Reynolds <m.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro & discovery - Private VPC follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier - good overview. As promised, here are the follow-up items we discussed on data handling and the Private/VPC deployment:

1) PII & data minimization
- Do you recommend client-side redaction before sending to Redwood?
- Does Redwood ever persist full-text inputs/outputs for hosted vs Private deployments?

2) Retention & logging
- What are the defaults for request logs, KV cache, and model telemetry?
- Can retention be configured per-tenant or per-route?

3) Data residency / egress controls
- For Private VPC, please confirm all inference traffic stays within our VPC/subnets.
- What control do we have over outbound egress (to download model weights, OS updates, telemetry)?

4) On-prem / air-gapped constraints
- We may need an air-gapped option for some workloads. Is there an offline installer or appliance model?

Can you capture the above in a short data-flow diagram and provide any sample security docs (SOC2, KMS/HSM notes)? Also we attached Acme's initial questionnaire - some items are highlighted.

Proposed next step: 30-45 minute technical follow-up with your infra lead. Availability next Wed/Thu.

Thanks,
Alice Singh
Head of Platform Security, AcmeHealth

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Singh <alice.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro & discovery - Private VPC follow-up

Hi Alice - great to meet you and thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and next steps at the bottom. I attached a concise VPC data-flow diagram (redwood-vpc-dataflow.pdf) and a filled copy of your questionnaire (acmehealth-data-questions.xlsx).

Quick answers:
- PII: We recommend client-side redaction where possible for sensitive fields. For Private/VPC deployments, by default Redwood does not exfiltrate customer payloads from the customer-managed network unless explicit egress is configured.
- Persistence: In Private deployments you control logs/retention. By default our platform can keep request logs for 30 days; KV cache (used for prefix caching to reduce cost) is configured to expire after 7 days by default but is adjustable. Hosted API defaults are more conservative for troubleshooting and retention - we can provide a configuration matrix.
- Retention/config: Retention is configurable per-tenant and can be scoped per-route in Dedicated/Private editions.
- Egress & residency: For Private VPC, inference traffic and model serving run within your VPC/subnets. Model weight provisioning requires an initial bootstrap (options: pull from a customer-controlled S3 with restricted IAM, or we can ship pre-baked weights via secure transfer for air-gapped installs). Outbound telemetry/updates are opt-in; you can block outbound access and still run inference locally.
- On-prem / air-gapped: We offer an offline installer & air-gap deployment path (requires coordination with our applied ML team and infra for model packaging). HSM/KMS integration is supported for key management.

Security artifacts we can share: SOC 2 summary, network hardening checklist, KMS integration doc, and a sample egress gating playbook.

Next steps:
- Technical follow-up call with our infra lead (Dev Patel) and applied ML (Jonas). I'm available Thu 18 Feb 10:00-12:00 PT or Fri 19 Feb 09:00-11:00 PT.
- I'll circulate the data-flow pdf and questionnaire and request your team's VPC CIDR + relevant firewall/proxy details before the call.

Let me know which slot works and any additional stakeholders to include.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-vpc-dataflow.pdf (diagram), acmehealth-data-questions.xlsx (filled)

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro & discovery - Private VPC follow-up

Hi Alice - quick technical notes ahead of the call. Adding a few clarifications to Marissa's summary:

- Egress control options:
  * No egress: For fully air-gapped installs we provide offline model packaging. Once installed, the runtime does not need outbound internet to serve inferences.
  * Egress gateway: For managed Private VPCs we can route all outbound traffic through a customer-provided NAT/proxy; telemetry and optional updates can be sent to whitelisted endpoints only.

- Model weights & provisioning:
  * Customer-pull: Customer grants the runtime access to an internal artifact store (S3/GCS on private link) from which weights are fetched during provisioning.
  * Offline transfer: For high-regulation customers we use signed bundles delivered via secure transfer; the runtime verifies signatures and stores weights in encrypted volume.

- Logs & KV cache:
  * Request logs are controllable; you can disable full payload logging and instead keep only metadata (timestamps, route ids, token counts).
  * KV cache is stored on local encrypted disk in Private deployments; retention policy is configurable.

- On-prem considerations:
  * Air-gapped customers must provide install window and bootstrap connectivity for license verification (we support short-lived, one-time verification tokens).
  * HSM/KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM via PKCS#11).

Action items for the call: please share
  - VPC CIDRs and subnet mapping
  - Any egress-proxy or firewall appliance IPs
  - Whether your cluster must be completely offline after install (air-gap) or allowed limited outbound to update endpoints

I'll be the technical lead on the follow-up. Happy to run a short demo of the runtime's network isolation and a tour of the retention config.

- Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

- For KV cache: any guidance on what types of state you expect to persist? E.g., do you cache raw prompt prefixes or only model-specific token states?
- We prefer the air-gap route for PHI workloads. Please include offline installer steps and expected lead times in the docs.

We can do the technical follow-up on Wed 17 Feb at 10:00 AM PT. Can you confirm a calendar invite and an agenda (30-45 mins)? Also we'll share our VPC CIDRs and a short network diagram prior to the call.
